Python and native Wasmtime share the pinned version; their library bytes and build/linkage identities are recorded separately and may differ. Native serial changes only compiler parallelism, not Wasm threads. Precompiled uses the native default configuration and an explicitly prepared, trusted local artifact. When supplied, the minimal companion runs artifacts from both backends prepared by the full host with --aot-profile minimal and default compiler parallelism. The minimal profile excludes exception handling and GC; every selected artifact must compile and qualify under that profile. Preparation includes fresh host launch, Wasm compilation, serialization and file writing. Guest source, Wasm and native-C artifact bytes are unchanged. After input hashes and artifact qualification, selected executable, Wasm and AOT inodes are fsynced, advised DONTNEED where supported, then sequentially read in 1 MiB blocks before warmups. Dependencies and shared libraries are outside this primary-file normalization. Phases run sequentially; runtime modes are shuffled within each example/round block. Separate preparation commands never overlap runtime sampling. No headline runner writes a timing file.", "note": "Complete preparation cost for trusted native artifacts; guest execution is separate.
